chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
'Do not drink water excessively, for indeed it is a source of every illness.'

key_terms.دَاءٍ: illness, disease, ailment; a broad term encompassing all forms of bodily sickness
key_terms.مَادَّةٌ: literally 'matter' or 'substance'; in the medical context of this hadith, it means 'source' or 'generator'—i.e., excessive water is that which generates or sustains illness in the body

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about drinking too much water?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises against excessive water consumption, stating that overdrinking is a source of every illness. This narration reflects early Islamic medical wisdom, consistent with the classical Galenic-Islamic medical tradition that cautioned against diluting the body's vital humors by excessive fluid intake. The hadith would have resonated with an audience familiar with Greco-Islamic medicine, which emphasized balance (mizan) in all bodily intake.
